title: A flat quasi-finite slice through a closed Cohen–Macaulay fibre point
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a flat morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-flat-morphism] locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. Let $s\in S$ and let $x$ be a closed point [def-weil-closed-points] of the scheme-theoretic fibre $X_s$ [def-pc-scheme-fibre]. Suppose that $R=\mathcal O_{X_s,x}$ is Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] and $\operatorname{depth}R=\dim R$ [def-weil-pbc-depth, def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]. Then there are a scheme $Z$, a morphism $i:Z\to X$, and a point $z\in Z_s$ such that $i(z)=x$, the composite $f\circ i:Z\to S$ is flat and locally of finite presentation, and $Z_s$ has exactly one point, namely $z$. Moreover $f\circ i$ is locally quasi-finite [pqf-def-quasifinite].

source.place: Tag 0570, label lemma-slice-CM, specialized to a globally flat morphism and forgetting regularity of the immersion in its conclusion

proof.text: For each $n\in\mathbf N$, let $P(n)$ assert: for every flat locally finitely presented $g:Y\to S$, $s\in S$, and closed $y\in Y_s$ whose local ring $A=\mathcal O_{Y_s,y}$ is Noetherian with $\dim A=n$ and $\operatorname{depth}A\ge n$, there are $i:Z\to Y$ and $z\in Z_s$ with $i_s(z)=y$, $Z_s=\{z\}$, and $g\circ i$ flat, locally finitely presented and locally quasi-finite. Prove all $P(n)$ by strong induction. Here $Z_s$ is the fibre of $g\circ i$, with projection $p_Z:Z_s\to Z$. For the item, $R$ is a nonzero local ring (its maximal ideal is proper), so [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-local-finite-krull-dimension] gives $\dim R\in\mathbf N$; the depth equality lets us apply $P(\dim R)$ to $f,s,x$.

source.place: Tag 0570, lemma-slice-CM, induction on fibre dimension; use the equivalent local-ring dimension parameter.

proof.text: For $P(0)$, the closed point $y$ and the locally finitely presented $g$ satisfy every hypothesis of [lem-trf-zero-dimensional-closed-fibre-open-slice]. Take $Z=V$, $i=j$, $z=v$. The child gives $j_s(v)=y$, hence $i_s(z)=y$, and $V_s=\{v\}$, hence $Z_s=\{z\}$. It also gives local quasi-finiteness and local finite presentation of $g\circ i$. Its conditional flatness applies because $g$ is flat. These are all conclusions of the induction claim.

For $P(d)$ with $d>0$, apply [lem-trf-cm-fibre-hypersurface-dimension-drop] to the flat locally finitely presented $g$, the closed $y\in Y_s$, and $A$ with $\dim A=d$ and $\operatorname{depth}A\ge d$. It supplies $D\to U\to Y$, a closed $y_D\in D_s$ over $y$, and a flat locally finitely presented $D\to S$. Set $A_D=\mathcal O_{D_s,y_D}$. The child's last assertion gives Noetherianity of this actual fibre local ring, $\dim A_D=d-1$, and $\operatorname{depth}A_D\ge d-1$, not merely these properties for an abstract quotient. As $d>0$ is an integer, $0\le d-1<d$. These are exactly the smaller-dimensional induction data, including when $d=1$.

source.place: Tag 0570, lemma-slice-CM, positive-dimensional cut and quotient (old steps 4--5 and the quotient part of 6).

proof.text: Write $k:D\to Y$ for $D\to U\to Y$ and $g_D=g\circ k$. Apply the uniform induction hypothesis to $g_D,s,y_D$: step 3 supplies its flatness, local finite presentation, and closed fibre point with Noetherian local ring of dimension $d-1\ge0$ and depth at least $d-1$, and $d-1<d$. Obtain $j:Z\to D$ and $z\in Z_s$ with $j_s(z)=y_D$, singleton fibre, and all three required properties for $g_D\circ j$. Put $i=k\circ j$. Associativity gives $g\circ i=g_D\circ j$; hence its fibre over $s$ and all three morphism properties are exactly those supplied by induction. The universal property of the fibre product identifies the induced map $i_s:Z_s\to Y_s$ with $k_s\circ j_s$: their projections to $Y$ are $k\circ j$ composed with the fibre projection, and their projections to $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)$ agree. Thus $i_s(z)=k_s(y_D)=y$. Writing $p_Y:Y_s\to Y$ for the fibre projection, this also gives $i(p_Z(z))=p_Y(y)$, exactly the point-image assertion in the item. This completes the induction.

source.place: Tag 0570, lemma-slice-CM, induction and composition of the resulting slice; regularity of the immersion is not required.

proof_origin.place: Tag 0570, lemma-slice-CM; induction on fibre local-ring dimension, using the depth >= dimension form of Cohen–Macaulayness and forgetting the regular-immersion conclusion.
